title: MDQ Specification Audit: essay
scope: The essay question type: `docs/question-types/essay.md` and `schema/essay.yaml`, read against `docs/references/grammar.md`, `docs/references/patterns.md`, `docs/question-types/question-base.md`, `docs/exam.md` and `docs/responses.md`. Earlier audits already settled the shared rules.
methodology:
The audit script `scripts/spec_audit.py` passed all 15 steps before the audit started: it compiles every Lark snippet, checks the Additional Rules tables against `docs/lint-codes.md` and the corpus, and checks the frontmatter tables against the schemas.

The lead auditor read `docs/question-types/essay.md` with the shared specs and recorded contradictions, ambiguities, omissions and inconsistencies. The audit focused on what is specific to essay: the `[essay]` tag, the `input` and `highlight` fields, the answer key section, the response and the manual grading. Edge cases were run through mdq-py to see how the reference implementation reads the text.

One subagent turned the essay grammar and the shared grammar into Lark and tested what they accept and reject. A second, independent subagent scanned the essay document and schema, ran each complete example through `mdq validate`, and checked the Additional Rules table against the MUST, SHOULD and MAY requirements of the text.

findings.title: Essay grammar rejects an indented [essay] tag and trailing spaces
findings.description: The rule has no `ws?` before or after the tag. Tested with Lark: `  [essay]`, `   [essay]`, `\t[essay]` and `[essay]  ` are all rejected. But question-base.md:219-220 says "a tag may be indented", and grammar.md:59-69 defines the leading `ws?` of a block as the CommonMark indentation of at most three spaces. The numeric and short-answer tag rules (numeric.md:75, short-answer.md:154) start with `ws?` and end with `ws?`; the essay rule does not. mdq-py accepts `  [essay]`, `   [essay]` and `[essay]  ` as essay bodies, and rejects `    [essay]` (code block), which matches the prose, not the grammar. The `ordering` rule (ordering.md:141) has the same gap; the ordering audit covers it.
findings.impact: A reader who follows the grammar rejects valid documents with an indented tag or trailing spaces; an implementation built from the grammar disagrees with mdq-py.
findings.fix: Write the rule as `essay : ws? "[essay]" ws?`, as the numeric and short-answer rules do.

findings.title: Essay grammar does not say it applies to a paragraph, so it accepts the content of a list item
findings.snippet: The body consists of a single `[essay]` tag.
findings.description: The grammar matches only the text `[essay]` and does not state the block that holds it. grammar.md:73-79 says a list-item grammar applies to the item content after the removal of the marker. With that reading, the content of `* [essay]` is `[essay]` and the grammar accepts it, while the Additional Rules table (essay.md:90) forbids the tag as a list item (`foreign-choice-marker`). The content of the heading `## [essay]` is also `[essay]`. mdq-py reads only a paragraph as the tag: `* [essay]` gives `foreign-choice-marker` and `## [essay]` gives a missing body. The grammar also does not say that the tag is the whole paragraph: `Describe the Pantanal.\n[essay]` (one paragraph) is rejected by mdq-py, and the spec settles this only by the word "single". The corpus fixes more cases that the Additional Rules table does not list: `essay-tag-with-text` (`[essay] com no máximo 200 palavras`) and `essay-tag-uppercase` (`[Essay]`) expect `parse-error`, and `essay-two-tags` expects `forbidden-block-element` in the epilogue.
findings.impact: The block context of the tag comes from implementation behavior and a footnote, not from the grammar.
findings.fix: State that the body is a paragraph whose only content is the rule, for example `essay_block : ws? "[essay]" ws? nl`, and that a list item or heading is not the tag. State that a later `[essay]` paragraph is a forbidden element of the epilogue, and list the parse errors in the Additional Rules table, as other types do.

findings.title: The answer key section has no grammar, and its heading variants and extent are not specified
findings.snippet: It starts with an `H2` heading with the text `## [answer-key]`
findings.description: The answer key section is defined only in prose; essay.md has no rule for it, unlike the `## [extra]` section of ordering (ordering.md:146: `"##" ws "[" "extra" "]" nl+ content`). The prose says both "an H2 heading" and "the text `## [answer-key]`", so it does not settle these inputs: the setext H2 `[answer-key]` + `---` (mdq-py accepts it as the answer key), `##   [answer-key]   ` (mdq-py accepts), `## [Answer-Key]`, `### [answer-key]` and `## [answer-key] Notes` (mdq-py rejects them as `forbidden-block-element` in the epilogue). The prose also does not say where the section ends or what blocks it may hold: mdq-py reads every block up to the end of the question, so a later `## Rubric` heading and its list are inside `answerKey`. Inside an exam the end is the next `===` or `---` block, which the text does not mention. The forbidden elements of question-base.md are not checked in the section either: mdq-py keeps an H1 and a second `[essay]` paragraph after the answer key as answer key text (`answerKey: "Key.\n\n[essay]"`), and prose after the answer key meant as epilogue goes into it. No example in examples/ has a heading, a bracketed paragraph or more prose after the answer key, or any heading form other than `## [answer-key]`.
findings.impact: Two implementations can split the same document into a different epilogue and answer key.
findings.fix: Add a grammar rule, for example `answer_key : "##" ws "[" "answer-key" "]" ws? nl md_block+`. State that the heading is an ATX H2 alone on its line (decide on the setext form; CommonMark reads both as H2), and that the section holds every block after it, headings included except H1, up to the end of the question (end of file, or the next block in an exam).

findings.title: SLUG accepts `essay`, so `[essay]` at the start of the first paragraph is a slug
findings.description: The slug rule (question-base.md:174-175, 197-199) reads a bracket at the start of the first paragraph as a slug when its content matches SLUG, and `essay` matches. No rule excludes the type tag names. So `[essay] Describe the Pantanal.` followed by `[essay]` is a question with id `essay` (mdq-py output: `{"type": "essay", "id": "essay", ...}`). A document whose first paragraph is only `[essay]` is either a slug-only stem paragraph or the body with no stem; the spec does not say which (mdq-py reads it as the body and reports a missing field).
findings.impact: Contrived inputs where the spec gives two readings of the same bracket.
findings.fix: State whether a type tag name such as `essay` can be a slug, and that a paragraph of only `[essay]` is always the essay tag.

findings.title: The response format of a "text" essay is not defined
findings.snippet:
"text" indicates that the response should be a rich text input, potentially
supporting markdown or other formatting.
findings.description: `input: text` asks for a rich text editor "potentially supporting markdown or other formatting", and `docs/responses.md:38` says the essay response is "the text the student wrote". Neither document says what the response string holds for a rich text editor: Markdown source, HTML, or text with the formatting removed. `input: code` and `input: plain` have no such doubt.
findings.impact: Two hosts that exchange responses (an LMS, a grader, an exporter) can store the same answer as Markdown in one and as HTML in the other. A renderer cannot tell which it received, and raw HTML in a response is also an injection risk when the host renders it as Markdown.
findings.fix: State in `docs/responses.md` and in Input that the response of every essay is a string, and that for `input: text` it is CommonMark source. A host whose editor produces HTML converts it before it stores the response. `plain` and `code` responses are verbatim text.

findings.title: An empty or repeated answer key section has no documented rule
findings.snippet: | answerKey | error    | blank-text                   | if defined, must have at least one visible character       |
findings.description: The Additional Rules table has no rule for a second `## [answer-key]` section, but `examples/invalid/essay-two-answer-keys.mdq.md` expects a `parse-error`. For a section with no content (`## [answer-key]` as the last line), the `blank-text` rule suggests an error, but mdq-py accepts the document and drops the field: the result has no `answerKey` and no error. The corpus already decides the empty case the other way: examples/valid/essay/empty-answer-key.mdq.md is valid and expects only `missing-answer-key`, while examples/invalid/model-only/essay-blank-answer-key.yaml is a `blank-text` error. So the rule that an empty Markdown section defines no answer key exists only in the corpus.
findings.impact: The corpus enforces a rule the spec does not state, and an empty section, which is almost always an unfinished question, passes with only the `missing-answer-key` info at most.
findings.fix: Add a rule for a second section (`parse-error`) to the table. For the empty section, two readings are defensible: (a) an empty section is an absent answer key, reported only as `missing-answer-key`, as the corpus decides (examples/valid/essay/empty-answer-key.mdq.md); (b) it is a defined but blank field, `blank-text`, as for `title:` with only spaces. Recommended: (a), since `## [answer-key]` with nothing after it is a common template placeholder, and state it in the text and the table.

findings.title: The text never maps the answer key section to the `answerKey` field
findings.description: The Answer key section describes the Markdown syntax but never states that its content becomes the `answerKey` field of the AST, nor how the blocks are joined into the string. The field name appears only in the Additional Rules table (lines 92 and 95) and in `schema/essay.yaml:41`. The document also has no YAML form of a parsed essay.
findings.impact: A reader of the Markdown spec cannot tell which field holds the answer key, or that it is a field of the body and therefore invalid in the frontmatter (`invalid-frontmatter-field`).
findings.fix: Add one sentence: the blocks of the section, without the heading, are the `answerKey` string, with the same normalization license as `stem` and `epilogue`. Add the YAML form of the example.

findings.title: The Grading section does not give the score range, automation or response
findings.description: The rules that apply to an essay are spread over other documents: the automation is `manual` (`question-base.md:280`), every response is pending (`responses.md:312-313`), the score is in [0, 1] (`exam.md:359`), the exam `grading` does not apply (`exam.md:359`), and the response is a string (`responses.md:190-204`). The essay document links to none of them, and the instructor's score range is stated only for fill-in blanks (`responses.md:320-321`). `ordering.md` has Automation and Response sections; essay does not.
findings.impact: A reader of the essay document cannot learn how an essay is scored or what its response looks like without reading three other documents.
findings.fix: Expand Grading: the automation is `manual`, every response is pending until the instructor gives a score in [0, 1], the exam `grading` does not apply and `penalty` does. Add a Response section that links to `responses.md`.

findings.title: A warning rule is written as "must"
findings.snippet: | highlight | warning  | ignored-highlight            | must be omitted unless `input` is "code"                   |
findings.description: The level is `warning`, which maps to SHOULD, but the rule says "must be omitted". Footnote 1 says only that the property is ignored, with no requirement level. `question-base.md` writes its warnings as "should" (`unsafe-id`: "should be url-safe"). The info rule `code-input-without-highlight` (essay.md:94) is not described in the prose either.
findings.impact: The table contradicts its own level, and a reader can take the rule as an error.
findings.fix: Write "should be omitted unless ..." in both tables, and in footnote 1 add that the property SHOULD be omitted.

findings.title: When the answer key may be shown to students is not defined
findings.snippet:
key section is optional and serves as a guide for the instructor to grade the 
responses and may be presented as feedback to the students.
findings.description: The answer key "may be presented as feedback", but the text does not say when (after the response, after grading, after the exam closes) or whether a host must hide it before. The other types define feedback that shows after grading; a pending essay "shows no feedback" (`responses.md:319-320`).
findings.impact: A host can show the model answer while the exam is open, and the rule that a pending response shows no feedback seems to forbid showing it at all until the instructor grades.
findings.fix: State that the answer key MUST NOT be shown to the student before they submit the response, and that it MAY be shown after, even while the response is pending.

findings.title: No fields for response size or attachments
findings.description: Essay has no field for a minimum or maximum length (words or characters), the size of the input box, or file attachments. Moodle essay questions have `responsefieldlines`, `minwordlimit`, `maxwordlimit` and `attachments`; the `mdq export` targets lose nothing today, but an import from Moodle drops them.
findings.impact: Authors write length limits in the stem (`essay-tag-with-text` shows the attempt), where no host can enforce them.
findings.fix: Decide whether MDQ covers these. If yes, add optional `minWords`/`maxWords` fields; if no, state that limits belong in the stem or in `meta`.

findings.title: Essay spec says both that essays may require and that they always use manual grading
findings.snippet: Essay questions are usually open-ended, and may require manual grading.
findings.description: Line 55 says essays "may require manual grading", which implies some are graded automatically. Line 82 and question-base.md:280 say essays are always graded manually (`manual` automation).
findings.impact: A reader can expect some automatic grading of essays, for example from the answer key.
findings.fix: Replace "may require manual grading" with a statement that every essay response is graded by the instructor.

findings.title: Essay places its answer key section after the epilogue, ordering places its sections before it
findings.snippet:
The answer key section is placed below the `[essay]` tag and any existing
epilogue block.
findings.description: Both types use `## [name]` sections after the body. In essay the epilogue comes before `## [answer-key]` (examples/valid/essay/epilogue-and-answer-key.mdq.md). In ordering the sections follow the content block directly and the epilogue comes after the last section; prose between the block and a section is a `parse-error`. question-base.md:4-6 and 264-265 describe the essay order (special sections after the epilogue), so ordering disagrees with the base, and the two types disagree with each other.
findings.impact: Authors must learn two placements for the same `## [name]` construct, and a parser cannot share the section logic.
findings.fix: Choose one placement for `## [name]` sections relative to the epilogue and use it in question-base.md, essay.md and ordering.md.
findings.conditions: An essay or ordering question with both an epilogue and a section.

findings.title: Essay `input` and ordering `content` hold the same code/text choice under different names
findings.description: Both fields select between `code` (paired with `highlight`, with the same `ignored-highlight` and `unknown-highlight-language` rules) and `text`. Essay calls the field `input` and adds `plain`; ordering calls it `content` and has no `plain`. The lint-codes.md row of `ignored-highlight` has to say "`input`/`content`".
findings.impact: Authors who write both types must remember two names for one concept.
findings.fix: Use one field name for the code/text choice in both types, or document why they differ.

findings.title: Exam rules about `---` and setext headings do not cover the essay answer key
findings.snippet:
Inside an exam, the epilogue of a question MUST NOT use `---` as a thematic
break.
findings.description: The exam rules name only the epilogue (and the stem and instructions for `setext-heading`). The answer key comes after the epilogue and is the last block of an essay in an exam, so a `---` in it has the same problem. mdq-py applies the epilogue rule to it: a `---` in the answer key gives `parse-error` with the message "a question's epilogue cannot use '---'", and a setext `[answer-key]` heading gives `setext-heading` at path `epilogue` while it parses as `answerKey`. The spec does not state either behavior and no example in examples/ covers it.
findings.impact: Implementations can accept a `---` in an answer key, and a later question then starts inside it.
findings.fix: Extend the exam rules to every block after the body, the answer key included.
findings.conditions: An essay with an answer key inside an exam.

findings.title: Essay spec does not say how footnotes resolve across the stem, epilogue and answer key
findings.snippet: The answer key section is placed below the `[essay]` tag and any existing
findings.description: Each part is stored as its own Markdown string. mdq-py accepts a stem with `[^1]` whose definition is in the answer key: the stem keeps a reference with no definition, and the definition is hidden with the answer key. The spec does not say if a footnote reference must be defined in the same field, and no example in examples/ covers it (examples/valid/essay/epilogue-starts-with-footnote.mdq.md only has an epilogue footnote).
findings.impact: The student view renders a dangling footnote, or a host that renders the whole document shows text from the answer key.
findings.fix: State that a footnote definition belongs to the field it is in, and lint a reference defined in another field.
findings.conditions: An essay that uses footnotes and has an answer key.

findings.title: schema/essay.yaml gives `highlight` a validation role the spec does not have
findings.snippet:
Programming language used for syntax highlighting and, where
          supported, validation.
findings.description: The schema says `highlight` is used for syntax highlighting "and, where supported, validation". essay.md:44-45 says only that it specifies the language for syntax highlighting. The spec does not define any validation of the response by language.
findings.impact: Hosts can reject responses that do not compile, which the spec does not permit or describe.
findings.fix: Remove the validation clause from the schema, or describe the behavior in essay.md.

findings.title: schema/essay.yaml rejects an empty `highlight`, the spec does not say so
findings.description: The schema sets `minLength: 1` on `highlight`, so `highlight: ""` is a `schema-error` (mdq-py confirms). essay.md does not state this constraint; question-base.md:366-367 says identifiers and syntax fields reject the empty string, but essay.md does not say that `highlight` is one.
findings.impact: Readers of essay.md cannot tell that an empty `highlight` is an error and not an ignored value.
findings.fix: Add the constraint to the essay frontmatter table or footnote [^1].

strengths.text: The essay tag literal `"[essay]"` agrees with the bracketed-tag rules of question-base.md:211-217: tested with Lark, it accepts `[essay]` and rejects `[ essay ]` (whitespace inside brackets), `[Essay]` (case), `[essay] write here`, `[essay]\nwrite here` (more than a single tag) and `[essay](http://x)` (a link). mdq-py gives the same result for each of these inputs.

The essay corpus covers the tag variants and misplacements: spaced, uppercase, NBSP-indented, indented, in a list, in a blockquote, with trailing text, repeated, and an answer key before the body or repeated.
schema/essay.yaml agrees with essay.md on the `input` enum and its default `text`, on `highlight` being ignored with a warning for non-code input, and on `answerKey` blank-text.

The essay lint codes in essay.md agree with docs/lint-codes.md in name, level and scope (`ignored-highlight`, `unknown-highlight-language`, `code-input-without-highlight`, `missing-answer-key`, `foreign-choice-marker`).
Both complete examples in essay.md (lines 7-11 and 63-78) validate with mdq-py with no error or warning.

risks: Essay looks like the simplest type, but most of its rules live in the corpus and in mdq-py, not in the text: the tag paragraph, the answer key section, its extent and its empty form.
The response of a rich text essay has no defined format, so two hosts can exchange the same answer as Markdown and as HTML.

recommendations.text: Define the `[essay]` paragraph and the answer key section in the grammar and the Additional Rules table.
Define the response format of each essay `input`.
Apply the mechanical fixes: `ws?` in the tag rule, "should" in the warning rules, the grading sentence of line 55, and the two `highlight` schema descriptions.
Use one placement for `## [name]` sections in essay and ordering, and extend the exam `---` rules to them.
Document essay grading, response and answer key visibility in essay.md.
Explain or unify essay `input` and ordering `content`.

issues.title: [Spec] Define the `[essay]` paragraph and the `## [answer-key]` section in the grammar
issues.summary: The essay grammar is one literal, and the answer key section has no grammar at all. What the tag paragraph is, how the answer key heading is spelled, where the section ends, what an empty or repeated section is, and which field it fills are known only from the corpus and mdq-py. Recommended: write `essay_block` and `answer_key` rules, state that the section runs to the end of the question and fills `answerKey`, document an empty section as an absent answer key (corpus behavior), a second section as `parse-error`, and that a footnote belongs to the field it is in. Decide whether a setext `[answer-key]` heading is valid (recommended: yes, as CommonMark reads it as H2) and whether type tag names can be slugs (recommended: yes, and a paragraph of only `[essay]` is always the tag).
acceptance: essay.md has grammar rules for the tag paragraph and the answer key section
The text states the extent of the section and that it fills `answerKey`
The Additional Rules table lists the second-section and tag-paragraph errors
The corpus has examples for a section with headings inside and for the empty section

issues.title: [Spec] Define the response format of a "text" essay
issues.summary: `input: text` is a rich text editor, but neither essay.md nor responses.md says whether the response string is Markdown, HTML or plain text. Options: (a) CommonMark source for `text`, verbatim text for `plain` and `code`; (b) leave it to the host. Recommended: (a), since MDQ is Markdown and a host with an HTML editor can convert.
acceptance: responses.md and essay.md state the format of the response for each `input`
A corpus response example exists for an essay

issues.title: [Spec] Document essay grading, response and answer key visibility in essay.md
issues.summary: The essay Grading section is one sentence. The automation, the pending state, the [0, 1] score range, the exam `grading` exclusion and the response shape live in three other documents, and the text does not say when the answer key can be shown. Recommended: add Automation and Response sections as ordering has, and state that the answer key MUST NOT be shown before the student submits and MAY be shown after, even while pending. Also decide whether MDQ covers response length limits (recommended: no; state that they go in the stem or `meta`).
acceptance: essay.md has Grading, Automation and Response sections with links to responses.md and exam.md
The text states when the answer key may be shown

issues.title: [Spec] Use one placement for `## [name]` sections relative to the epilogue
issues.summary: Essay puts its answer key after the epilogue; ordering puts its sections right after the body and the epilogue after them. The exam rules about `---` and setext headings name only the epilogue, although mdq-py applies them to the answer key. Options: (a) sections always after the epilogue, as question-base.md describes; (b) sections always right after the body. Recommended: (a), since it agrees with question-base.md and the essay corpus; ordering then follows in its own audit. Extend the exam rules to every block after the body.
acceptance: question-base.md, essay.md and ordering.md state the same placement
exam.md applies the `---` and setext rules to the answer key
A corpus exam example has an essay with an answer key

issues.title: [Spec] Use one field name for the code/text choice of essay and ordering
issues.summary: Essay `input` and ordering `content` select the same `code`/`text` mode, with the same `highlight` rules. Options: (a) keep both and document why (essay describes the editor, ordering describes the lines); (b) rename one. Recommended: (a), since the meanings differ (`plain` exists only for an editor) and a rename breaks documents; add one sentence to each document.
acceptance: essay.md and ordering.md explain the relation between `input` and `content`, or one field is renamed with a changelog entry
